**Notice:** *In this assignment, all the plot should have title, caption, and axis labels. *

1. Use the dataset by of covid 19 by WHO at https://covid19.who.int/WHO-COVID-19-global-data.csv. Find the three countries with the most numbers of deaths by Covid-19. 

Hint: 

-  Use `filter` to select the most current date 

-  Pipe with `arrange(-Cumulative_deaths)` to rank the data by the number of cumulative deaths

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

df <- read_csv("https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/WHO-COVID-19-global-data.csv")
str(df)
```

```{r}
df |> 
  filter(Date_reported == max(Date_reported)) |> 
  arrange(-Cumulative_deaths)
```

**The top 3 countries with the most cumulative deaths are the US, Brazil, and India.**

2. Use `transition_reveal` to make a plot revealing the number of deaths in the three countries with the most numbers of deaths

```{r}
library(gganimate)
df |> 
  filter(Country_code %in% c("US", "BR", "IN")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = Cumulative_deaths, x = Date_reported, color = Country)) +
  geom_line() +
  transition_reveal(Date_reported) +
  labs(x='Date Reported', 
       y = 'Cumulative Deaths', 
       color='Country', 
       title = 'Cumulative Deaths in the US, Brazil, and India Over Time', 
       caption = 'The US has more cumulative deaths than Brazil and India consistently over time.')
```


3. Create the new variable (column) `death_per_cases` recording the number of deaths per cases (Hint: divide cumulative deaths by cumulative cases).  What are the three countries with the highest deaths per cases? 

```{r}
df <- df |> mutate(death_per_cases = (Cumulative_deaths / Cumulative_cases))
df |> filter(Date_reported == max(Date_reported)) |> arrange(-death_per_cases)
```

**Yemem, Sudan, and Syrian Arab Republic are the top 3 countries with the most amount of deaths per cases on the most current date in the dataset.**

4. Use `transition_reveal` to make a plot revealing the number of deaths per cases of the US, Italy and Mexico. 

```{r}
df |> 
  filter(Country_code %in% c("US", "IT", "MX")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = death_per_cases, x = Date_reported, color = Country)) +
  geom_line() +
  transition_reveal(Date_reported) +
  labs(x='Date Reported', 
       y = 'Death per Cases', 
       color='Country', 
       title = 'Death per Cases Rate in the US, Italy, and Mexico.', 
       caption = 'Mexico has the highest death per cases rate out of these 3 countries.')
```


5. Import the following data https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owid/covid-19-data/master/public/data/vaccinations/vaccinations.csv

```{r}
df1 <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owid/covid-19-data/master/public/data/vaccinations/vaccinations.csv")
head(df1)
```

Use `transition_reveal` to plot the total vaccinations per hundred by level of income. Hint: the levels of income are identified in the `location` variable. Put a short comment on the caption of the plot. 

```{r}
table(df1$location)
```

```{r}
df1 |> 
  filter(str_detect(location, "income")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = total_vaccinations_per_hundred, x = date, color = location)) +
  geom_line() +
  transition_reveal(date) +
  labs(x = 'Date',
       y = 'Total Vaccinations per Hundred',
       color = 'Income Level',
       title = 'Total Vaccinations per Hundred by Income Level',
       caption = 'Higher income countries get vaccinated at a faster rate than lower income countries.')
```
